Kim Sung-hoon, CEO of Upstage, enters a hotel in Seoul on the 19th of last month to meet with AMD CEO Lisa Su. Yonhap News

Upstage announced Wednesday it has completed a 180 billion won ($126 million) first tranche of its Series C funding round.

The investment values Upstage at over 1 trillion won, making it the first South Korean startup developing generative artificial intelligence services and AI models to achieve unicorn status.

The funding brings Upstage's cumulative investment to approximately 400 billion won. The company plans to use the capital to expand GPU infrastructure for advancing AI models including its proprietary AI foundation model project, recruit top talent domestically and internationally, and develop market channels in the United States, Japan and other overseas markets.

The funding round was led by Sagemaker Partners, a Silicon Valley-based global venture capital firm. Sagemaker Partners has been an early investor that has participated in follow-on investments throughout Upstage's funding history. Major institutional investors including Premier Partners, Shinhan Venture Investment and Mirae Asset Venture Investment also made follow-on investments. Axiom Asia and other global investors, along with Hyundai Motor, Kia and Woori Venture Partners, joined as new investors.

Upstage provides industry-specific AI solutions powered by its self-developed large language model "Solar" and document processing AI "Document Parse." The company's revenue has grown more than 130 percent annually, reaching 24.8 billion won last year. Upstage plans to launch the second tranche of its Series C funding round soon.

"We will prove ourselves through revenue by advancing our proprietary AI models to be competitive not only in Korea but in global markets," Upstage CEO Kim Sung-hoon said.
